evals.name: sql-review-adaptive-intake
evals.prompt:
quick sanity check before my screen thursday. i wrote this to get the latest status per order and my teammate says its fine but idk

```sql
SELECT o.order_id, o.status, o.updated_at
FROM orders o
JOIN (
  SELECT order_id, MAX(updated_at) AS mx
  FROM orders
  GROUP BY order_id
) l ON o.order_id = l.order_id AND o.updated_at = l.mx
```

would this pass at a real DE interview or would they tear it apart
evals.expected_output: An immediate strict review of the query (not an intake questionnaire) that catches the duplicate-row bug when updated_at ties, gives a corrected ROW_NUMBER version, names the interview risk, and ends with a concrete next drill.

assertions.text: Reviews the query immediately instead of opening with an intake questionnaire
Catches that the self-join returns duplicate rows when two rows share the same max updated_at
Supplies a corrected query using ROW_NUMBER / QUALIFY / DISTINCT ON
Opens a modes/ file from the skill library
Opens a SQL-specific docs/ or practice/sql/ file
Ends with a concrete next drill or action

evals.name: roadmap-context-already-given
evals.prompt: ive got 2 years as a data analyst (mostly sql + some python scripting), interviewing for DE roles in about 6 weeks. spark is easily my weakest area, ive barely touched it. realistically 10-12 hrs a week. where do i start?
evals.expected_output: A prioritized 6-week roadmap that uses the experience, timeline, weak area and hours the user already supplied instead of re-asking them. Should push back if 6 weeks is tight, prioritize SQL, and give a first concrete task.

assertions.text: Does not re-ask for experience, timeline, weak area or study hours the user already gave
Produces a week-by-week plan spanning the stated 6 weeks
Puts SQL ahead of Spark and explains why, rather than leading with the self-declared weak area
Opens modes/roadmap-mode.md
Opens a roadmap template or roadmap doc
Gives a first concrete task to start on now

evals.expected_output: An actual interview round: a scoped realtime scenario, requirements the candidate must clarify, and a handoff back to them to answer. Should NOT dump a full model solution up front.

Presents a scoped realtime design scenario with constraints
Ends by handing control to the candidate with an explicit ask

evals.name: deep-topic-rows-vs-range
evals.prompt: i keep getting confused between ROWS and RANGE in window frames. bombed this in an interview last week, they asked for a running total and there were duplicate dates in the data. explain it properly
evals.expected_output: A precise explanation of the ROWS vs RANGE distinction, specifically why RANGE collapses peer rows with duplicate dates and gives a different running total than ROWS, with an example, the interview framing, and a drill.

assertions.text: Explains that RANGE treats tied ORDER BY values as peers and includes all of them in the frame
Explains that ROWS counts physical rows regardless of ties
Connects the distinction to the duplicate-date running total the user actually got wrong
Opens practice/sql/window-functions.md or docs/sql-interview-guide.md
Shows a worked example with the differing outputs side by side
Ends with a drill or practice task

evals.name: scope-boundary-production-work
evals.prompt: were standing up a new ingestion pipeline at work, kafka -> s3 -> snowflake, and i need to pick the partitioning strategy for the s3 landing zone. what should i go with?
evals.expected_output: Engages usefully but reframes toward the interview-relevant version (how to reason about and defend a partitioning choice) rather than either refusing or silently becoming a production consulting session.

assertions.text: Engages with the substance instead of refusing the question
Reframes toward the interview-relevant version rather than becoming a production consulting session
Names real partitioning trade-offs (date/hour granularity, small-file problem, cardinality)
